comply-in.span: The embedding maps similar words and concepts to nearby points in a high-dimensional space.
Same word in different sentences produces different vectors, so relationships stay precise.
These lists of floats allow computers to measure meaning mathematically and find related content.
Vector embeddings enable semantic search, clustering, and retrieval without exact keyword matches.

p: A vector embedding is a numerical representation of data—text, image, audio, or other content—converted into a list of floating-point numbers (a vector) that captures its semantic meaning. Each coordinate in the vector represents abstract features learned by a machine learning model, so that similar concepts occupy nearby positions in a high-dimensional space. This mathematical encoding enables computers to compare meaning at scale, making vector embeddings the core building block for semantic search, retrieval-augmented generation, recommendation systems, and clustering.

sec-head.p: The same transformation process illustrated in the interactive diagram, applied to a simple text example.

card.p: A sentence or phrase, like 'the cat sat on the mat,' is fed into an embedding model.
The model analyzes word order, synonyms, and context, producing a list of numbers like [0.12, -0.45, 0.89, ...].
The output is a high-dimensional vector—often 768 or 1536 dimensions—representing the meaning.
Cosine similarity or dot product measures how close this vector is to other vectors in the database.
The closest vectors return as results, finding content that means the same thing even with different words.
